blocks.value: **Nested control structures** are control statements placed within another. They can be nested to many levels. When nesting, make sure the start and end braces are placed correctly.
A for loop nested in an if...else

**The inner loop completes entirely for each single iteration of the outer loop.** The outer loop runs 10 times; the inner runs 10 times per outer iteration; the `print` executes 100 times. The `System.out.println()` after the inner loop ends the row, without it, all 100 numbers land on one line.
That structure, outer loop for rows, inner loop for columns, a newline between, is the pattern for every grid, table, and shape you will ever print.

Trace the `continue` carefully: on invalid input it jumps back to the `while` condition, skipping the "Repeat the program?" prompt entirely. The user is silently asked for the range again, which is the intent, but only because `continue` was placed deliberately.
